repair.mechanism: assemble_docket == assemble() (src/resextract/docket/assemble.py:1150; imported as assemble_docket at src/resextract/docket/materialize.py:106, the entry point called at materialize.py:2121). Its render-side cap _cap_uncapped_claims (assemble.py:1103, invoked at assemble.py:1244) reads the passed CONFIRMS, sees producer='unknown' (store.producer_is_model False), and re-renders EXTENDS with the reason recorded on Claim.verdict_reason (assemble.py:1136-1145). materialize._claim_standing (materialize.py:1609) is the same rule but is MemberSpec-typed and cannot be called without fabricating a member row (assemble.py:1117-1119), so the render cap is the honest route. No store interaction in assemble().
repair.exact_call: from resextract.docket.assemble import assemble, material_report_from_docket; m=json.load(MANIFEST); lane={**m['lane'],'status':m['status']}; assemble(docket_dir, lane=lane, claims=m['claims'], material_report=material_report_from_docket(docket_dir), target_meta=m['target'], freshness=m['freshness'], generated_at=m['generated_at'], model='', status='draft', producer='replay', status_reason=m['status_reason']) -- every input is the manifest's own recorded value, so nothing else can move. Rehearsed on a copy under state/verify/U5.27/rehearsal/ before the single real application.
repair.hand_edited_note: MANIFEST.json and CLAIMS.md were written ONLY by assemble(); the standing was never edited by hand. After the path ran, the render had also appended an assembly line to HISTORY.md and created a NEW ITEM.md.r5 (assemble()'s own ITEM.md preservation rotation; r1-r4 already existed) -- the natural render raised the verified banner-file count 15->16. Those two bookkeeping side effects were reverted/removed (HISTORY.md restored from backup; ITEM.md.r5 deleted) so the artifact diff is claim-only. ITEM.md.r5 is referenced nowhere in the manifest ('ITEM.md.r' not in MANIFEST.json -> False), so no dangling reference was left.

evidence.residual: Three residuals, none a re-damage. (1) 0 of 8 material items record a non-null blob_sha: every one is resolved_from='working_tree', so the material is pinned by sha256 of the copied bytes but not to a git blob -- the bytes cannot be re-fetched from a commit. (2) The file-fact standing gap still applies and is now VISIBLE: C-curated is kind='file-fact' (five files copied from the target at a recorded HEAD) and its honest state is now 'EXTENDS with a cap note', because there is still no distinct standing for mechanically-verified facts -- the cap note says why CONFIRMS was refused but does not express 'these bytes were hash-verified'. The verify_docket message itself names this as the alternative remedy. (3) The state.sqlite `dockets` row for duval-replay-material was deliberately NOT updated (a store write was forbidden and would have invalidated four siblings); the dashboard reads MANIFEST.json from disk, so the artifact is honest, but if that row mirrors claim standing it is now stale relative to the manifest. Also: HISTORY.md carries no record of this repair, because that line was reverted to keep the artifact diff claim-only -- the repair's provenance is this handoff plus the claim's own verdict_reason.
